title: Online scams a national security matter – ASEAN, US

blocks.text: Stock image of an attempted scam.

MANILA, Philippines — The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the United States urged governments to recognize online scams as a security matter that needs public-private partnership to combat the transnational organized criminal networks that may be behind the illegal activity.

On Tuesday, leaders of the ASEAN and the US adopted the Statement on 10 Public-Private Partnership Principles for Tackling Online Scams, which highlights shared interest in combating online scams, placing the disruption of criminal networks and the protection of victims as priorities.

“Public-private collaboration can be at its most efficient when it leverages existing frameworks to ensure that online scams, and the trafficking in persons that fuels them, are addressed at the highest levels of policymaking,” the statement read.

“Any public-private collaboration would aim to enhance safeguards to protect users from scams consistent with domestic law, raise awareness and facilitate information sharing to dismantle online scam compounds, [therefore] addressing human trafficking tied to forced criminality and disrupting illicit financial activity,” it noted.
